title: NanoTag - an IgG-free method for mapping DNA-protein interactions
authors: Maria A. Dimitriu; Rodrigo G. Arzate-Mejía; Leonard C. Steg; Pierre-Luc Germain; Isabelle M. Mansuy
one_liner_zh: 该文介绍一种基于纳米抗体的无IgG染色质 profiling 方法 NanoTag，用于绘制 DNA-蛋白互作图谱，虽涉及转录因子（Nanog、CTCF）与 DNA 结合，但核心是实验方法开发，无 AI 或物理模拟建模，仅部分相关。
abstract: Genome-wide profiling of DNA-protein interactions in cells can provide important information about mechanisms of gene regulation. Most current methods for genome-wide profiling of DNA-bound proteins, such as ChIP-seq and CUT&Tag, use conventional IgG antibodies to bind target protein(s), which limits their applicability to targets for which high affinity and high specificity antibodies are available. Here we describe NanoTag, a novel method derived from CUT&Tag that is IgG-free and uses a nanobody to profile DNA-protein interactions. NanoTag is based on an anti-GFP nanobody-Tn5 transposase fusion that allows mapping GFP-tagged proteins associated with chromatin in a fast and cost-effective manner. We demonstrate the utility of NanoTag by profiling the histone mark H3K4me3 via its binding partner TATA box-binding protein-associated factor 3 (TAF3) and the transcription factors Nanog and CTCF in mouse embryonic stem cells expressing GFP-tagged targets. For the targets examined, NanoTag data shows high correlation to CUT&Tag data and displays a similarly high signal-to-noise ratio. Overall, NanoTag provides a flexible, IgG-free and cost-effective method to generate high resolution DNA-binding profiles in cells or tissues.
abstract_zh: 对细胞中DNA-蛋白质相互作用的全基因组分析可提供关于基因调控机制的重要信息。目前大多数用于全基因组分析DNA结合蛋白的方法，如ChIP-seq和CUT&Tag，使用常规IgG抗体来结合目标蛋白，这限制了它们对可获得高亲和力和高特异性抗体的靶标的适用性。在此，我们描述了NanoTag，一种源自CUT&Tag的新方法，该方法无需IgG，并使用纳米抗体来剖析DNA-蛋白质相互作用。NanoTag基于抗GFP纳米抗体-Tn5转座酶融合体，能够以快速且经济高效的方式定位与染色质相关的GFP标记蛋白。我们通过在小鼠胚胎干细胞中表达GFP标记靶标，利用其结合伙伴TATA盒结合蛋白相关因子3（TAF3）以及转录因子Nanog和CTCF来剖析组蛋白标记H3K4me3，从而展示了NanoTag的实用性。对于所检查的靶标，NanoTag数据与CUT&Tag数据显示出高度相关性，并表现出同样高的信噪比。总体而言，NanoTag提供了一种灵活、无IgG且经济高效的方法，用于在细胞或组织中生成高分辨率的DNA结合图谱。
